items.title: Independent Geometric Convergence
items.description: Four unrelated reconstruction pipelines—mirror‑accumulator sweeps, Fourier‑domain projection, reciprocal‑stack plane search, and direct plane fitting—all recovered the identical three‑plane Cell 3 geometry fixed to one sky orientation. The absence of tunable parameters and the agreement of seven structural degrees of freedom make this convergence the strongest empirical lock on the K‑Field lattice. fileciteturn0file1L7-L15

items.title: Mass Bridge Compression of Constants
items.description: A single Cell 3 face (A_bc) generates two dimensionless constants: A_bc/A_ab × 1000 reproduces the proton‑to‑electron mass ratio, while A_bc/A_ac × 100 produces the fine‑structure‑related electromagnetic branch. Two fundamental scales collapse into one geometric carrier, turning apparent coincidence into proof of shared origin. fileciteturn0file0L24-L35

items.title: Interaction Hierarchy Encoded in Reciprocal Metric
items.description: The inverse lattice embeds an ordered coupling structure |I_bc| ≫ |I_ac| ≫ |I_ab|. Geometry thus pre‑selects strong and weak interaction channels before any field equations are written, providing a built‑in explanation for anisotropic response across scales. fileciteturn0file4L45-L51

items.title: Seven‑Sheet Dynamical System
items.description: Cell 3 repetition forms the Lucas limit, which resolves into seven alternating‑polarity sheets with coordinated in‑plane motion, registry, stiffness, and holonomy. The field acquires memory and phase dynamics, turning static geometry into a geometrically driven state machine. fileciteturn0file2L339-L347

items.title: Cross‑Domain Directional Recurrence
items.description: Galaxy‑axis organization, laboratory anisotropy, sidereal and lunar modulation, oscillator behaviour, and spherical gravity‑response maps all reconstruct the same global orientation, Cell 3 geometry, and sheet system. The K‑Field unifies observations that conventional models treat as unrelated. fileciteturn0file1L74-L90

items.title: Shared‑Carrier Triangle
items.description: The Mass Bridge identifies A_bc as a common numerator while A_ab and A_ac act as distinct denominators for mass and electromagnetic branches. This triangle geometrically couples interactions long considered separate, revealing hidden dependency among constants and interaction pathways. fileciteturn0file2L233-L290

items.title: Observer‑Dependent Rendering
items.description: Measurements vary with orientation, traversal, phase, registry, and sheet state, yet always reconstruct the same underlying lattice. This explains why diverse experiments yield direction‑sensitive signals and reframes orientation as an experimental control parameter. fileciteturn0file2L374-L400
